findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten the `grep` AC to check that `bedrock:Converse` does not appear as a granted *action* (not in comments), e.g. `grep -rn 'bedrock:Converse' infra/terraform/ | grep -v '^[^:]*:#'` or scope it to the `actions = [...]` block only.
evidence: infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf:14: # ACTION NAME: `bedrock:InvokeModel` — NOT `bedrock:Converse`.
infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf:18: # API. `bedrock:Converse` does exist as a distinct, simulatable IAM action
grep -rn 'bedrock:Converse' infra/terraform/ will emit two hits from comments, making the 'is empty' assertion a false failure
findings.finding: The AC `grep -rn 'bedrock:Converse' infra/terraform/` will produce non-empty output and therefore appear to FAIL, because iam_s7.tf contains the literal string 'bedrock:Converse' in comment lines (lines 14 and 18 of iam_s7.tf explain why that action name is NOT granted). The AC is semantically correct in intent — verify the action isn't granted — but the grep test as written cannot distinguish a comment from a grant.
scenarios: An operator running the AC verbatim gets non-empty output and incorrectly concludes the grant is wrong, or wastes time debugging a passing grant.
Automated CI running the grep check fails the story even though no Converse action is granted.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the AC with: "`grep -rn '"bedrock:Converse"' infra/terraform/` is empty` (double-quoted string match targets only HCL string literals, not comment prose), or use `grep -v '#'` to strip comment lines before checking.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten AC8's grep to match only policy action statements, not comments — e.g. scope it to the `actions` blocks with `grep -A20 'actions = \[' infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf | grep 'bedrock:Converse'`, or restate the AC as 'no `bedrock:Converse` appears in any `actions` list in `infra/terraform/`' so the explanatory comments are not required to be absent.
evidence: infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf:14: `# ACTION NAME: \`bedrock:InvokeModel\` — NOT \`bedrock:Converse\``
infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf:18: `# API. \`bedrock:Converse\` does exist as a distinct, simulatable IAM action`
The grep tests for any string occurrence, not for occurrences in the `actions = [...]` stanza or outside comments; both comment hits will produce output and the AC will appear to fail.
The intent of the AC is clearly to assert the action is not GRANTED, but the mechanism (grep for the string) does not distinguish comments from policy statements.
findings.finding: AC8's grep command (`grep -rn 'bedrock:Converse' infra/terraform/`) will produce non-empty output on the already-committed `iam_s7.tf`, because that file contains the string 'bedrock:Converse' in two comment lines (lines 14 and 18) explaining why the wrong action must NOT be granted. The AC will therefore falsely fail — not because Converse is granted, but because the grep matches comments.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC8: `grep -rn 'bedrock:Converse' infra/terraform/` is empty
scenarios: An executor runs `grep -rn 'bedrock:Converse' infra/terraform/` expecting empty output; gets two comment-line hits from iam_s7.tf; reports AC8 as failing; wastes time investigating a non-issue or strips the explanatory comments to make the AC pass (losing the institutional memory the plan deliberately embedded).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the AC line with: `- [ ] \`grep -rn 'bedrock:Converse' infra/terraform/ | grep -v '^[^:]*:#'\` is empty — Converse must not appear as a granted action (comment-only occurrences are expected and intentional)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] If the hop-limit contingency fires, specify the ADR 0046 entry's content using the ADR's existing schema — state the limitation (IMDS reachable from all bridge containers), the bounding control (default-bridge scope, first-party containers only, no untrusted workloads, existing `.env` secret access), the authority tier (infrastructure credential tier), and a deferred-hardening item (e.g. isolate compose services into named per-service networks); also explicitly affirm in the plan that gerrit and opcert acquiring `bedrock:InvokeModel` capability is an accepted outcome.
evidence: Plan: 'The exposure that raises is bounded and stated plainly: infra/compose/docker-compose.yml defines no networks: section, so gerrit, review-bot, and opcert already share one default bridge, and all three are first-party rebar components that already receive instance-role-derived secrets through the .env'
ADR 0046 L1–L5 each carry: Limitation / Why acceptable / Authority tier / Deferred hardening — the plan's contingency exception entry has none of these
Plan: 'record the exception in docs/adr/0046-security-posture-and-accepted-limitations.md' — no content schema given
ABSENCE: the plan does not affirm that gerrit and opcert containers calling bedrock:InvokeModel is explicitly accepted, only that the blast radius is bounded
findings.finding: Under the hop-limit contingency, the plan notes that raising `http_put_response_hop_limit` to 2 widens IMDS reachability to all containers on the shared bridge (gerrit, opcert) and argues this is bounded because they are first-party components, but it does not explicitly DECLARE that those containers acquiring the new `bedrock:InvokeModel` capability is an accepted outcome. The planned ADR 0046 update is also underspecified: ADR 0046's current structure covers L1–L5 signing/attestation limitations with a defined schema (limitation / bounding control / authority tier / deferred hardening), and the plan does not specify what the hop-limit exception entry's bounding control, authority tier, and deferred-hardening items should be.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Contingency, decided in advance' paragraph; Scope — 'docs/adr/0046-security-posture-and-accepted-limitations.md'; AC 'if the contingency fired'
scenarios: Contingency fires; ADR 0046 gets a vague one-liner rather than the structured accepted-limitation entry the ADR's schema demands; a future auditor cannot determine whether the hop-limit widening was a deliberate bounded trade-off or an unreviewed oversight.

Gerrit container is compromised; attacker uses IMDS (now reachable at hop-limit 2) to obtain the instance role and call bedrock:InvokeModel — the plan argues this is bounded but never records it as an accepted limitation with a named bounding control.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Scope entry for `docs/adr/0046-security-posture-and-accepted-limitations.md`, add a sentence specifying the new ADR limitation entry's four fields: 'L6 — Raised IMDS hop limit widens Bedrock-capable credentials to all bridge containers. Bounding control: all containers are first-party rebar workloads sharing the existing .env secret trust boundary; no untrusted workloads on the bridge. Authority tier: infrastructure credential tier only (no signing authority change). Deferred hardening: [ticket] — isolate compose services into named networks so the hop-limit change can be reverted.'
